mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last four weekly means (-32.9 to -26.7), an unbroken momentum trend; the same autoregressive drift persists for at least four more weeks, so the next-28-day mean exceeds the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly mean rose monotonically from -32.9 at t-3w to -26.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the last-28-day mean of -29.7.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT (-33.9 to -30.6, four consecutive weekly gains) proxies restored commuting and discretionary trip-making; transit recovery leads store footfall by roughly two weeks, so RETAIL_REC keeps climbing over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -33.9 at t-3w to -30.6 at t-0w with no negative week
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below -29.7.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is positive and rising (+0.9 to +3.7) while RETAIL_REC stays below -25; the persistent essentials tilt shows discretionary spend is still being withheld, so RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean stays below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean prints above +3.0 while RETAIL_REC remains below -25.0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +3.7 at t-0w versus RETAIL_REC at -26.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds -26.7 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above +3.0.

mechanism_narrative: Policy rollback that lifts transit capacity becomes visible when TRANSIT crosses above -30 percent of baseline; that crossing is followed by four weeks of release-driven retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -30.6 at t-0w sits only 0.6 points below the -30.0 crossing
failure_condition: Within two weeks of TRANSIT printing above -30.0, RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean falls below -29.7.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM at or above +2 combined with RESIDENTIAL falling from 11.9 to 10.6 means routine errands are moving back out of the home; the joint condition lifts RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.9 at t-3w to 10.6 at t-0w while GROCERY_PHARM rose to +3.7
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is at or above +2 and RESIDENTIAL is at or below +11.9 jointly, RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is below -29.7 in the majority of cases.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES gains have collapsed to +0.1 and +0.3 points per week (-21.1 to -18.7), so the commuter channel that fed weekday retail footfall is saturated; incremental RETAIL_REC gains stall and the next-28-day mean does not beat the last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change at or below +0.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly change decelerated from +2.0 points to +0.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds -26.7 even though WORKPLACES weekly change stays at or below +0.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovery to -13.4 outpaces RETAIL_REC recovery, showing discretionary time reallocating to outdoor leisure during the early-summer season; that reallocation caps indoor retail spending, so RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung +9.9 points from t-3w to t-0w versus +6.2 points for RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds -26.7 while PARKS stays above -15.0.

mechanism_narrative: A joint weekly move of TRANSIT up at least 1.0 point and RESIDENTIAL down at least 0.3 point marks substitution from staying home to travelling; this interaction predicts a one-week-lagged pickup that carries RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change at or above +1.0 point and RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change at or below -0.3 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows TRANSIT +1.4 points week-on-week alongside RESIDENTIAL -0.7 points
failure_condition: In weeks meeting the joint trigger, RETAIL_REC's next 7-day mean is lower than the prior 7-day mean more than half the time.
